cases.exposure_context_quote: A 45-year-old farmer with a body mass index = 22.1 (BMI = weight (kg)/height2 (m)) who was referred to the poisoning emergency center of Khorshid Hospital affiliated to Isfahan University of Medical Sciences about 6 days after the skin exposure through accidental spraying PQ 20% solution on his face and body.
cases.agent_quote: skin exposure through accidental spraying PQ 20% solution on his face and body
cases.route: dermal (accidental spraying on face and body; possible oral/mucosal contact with dysphagia)
cases.circumstance: accidental spraying of paraquat while working as a farmer; lack of protective equipment and no early body washing

symptoms.quote: He suffered from dysphagia, two episodes of hemoptysis containing clear blood clots, and respiratory distress which was started 3 days after exposure.
He suffered from dysphagia, two episodes of hemoptysis containing clear blood clots, and respiratory distress which was started 3 days after exposure.
heart rate, 107/min; respiratory rate, 30/min; blood pressure, 111/50 mm Hg; and O2 saturation, 52% which reached 91% with a bag valve mask.

symptoms.finding: second- and third-degree skin burns and multiple ulcers (face, mouth, neck, shoulders, axillae, elbows, trunk, hands, feet)
symptoms.quote: the patient was confused and he had second- and third-degree burns and multiple ulcers focusing on the body (face and around and in the mouth, forehead, neck, shoulders and axillary, elbows, trunk, hands, and feet) with yellow and green serous discharge.

symptoms.finding: confusion / decreased level of consciousness (GCS 4/15 later)
symptoms.quote: The level of patients’ consciousness decreased 16 h after admission with GCS 4/15
Physical examination of the lungs showed a decrease in the sound of the left lung.
The volume of urine was reduced and changed to brown.
In the HRCT, alveolar opacity by air bronchograms of both lungs with evidence of acute respiratory syndrome was seen.

cases.time_to_care: admitted to hospital 6 days after first contact

labs.name: urine sodium dithionate test
labs.quote: the urine sodium dithionate test for PQ on the first day at admission was strongly positive and defined as purple-colored urine.

labs.name: liver enzymes, urea, creatinine
labs.quote: In the initial tests of the patient, an increase in blood liver enzymes, urea, creatinine, as well as respiratory acidosis in the venous blood gas analysis was seen.

labs.name: venous blood gas
labs.quote: as well as respiratory acidosis in the venous blood gas analysis was seen

treatment.name: fluid hydration and oxygen supplement
treatment.quote: The patient was treated with fluid hydration, oxygen supplement, antioxidants

treatment.name: Vitamin E 300 units daily IM for 2 days; Vitamin C 2 g IV then 150 mg/h daily infusion for 2 days; N-acetylcysteine 300 mg/kg/day IV for 1 day
treatment.quote: antioxidants including Vitamin E 300 units daily for 2 days (Osvah Pharmaceutical Company, Tehran, Iran) intramuscular, Vitamin C 2 g intravenous (IV) infusion, and then 150 mg/h daily infusion for 2 days

treatment.name: methylprednisolone 1 g IV first day then 500 mg daily for 3 days
treatment.quote: methylprednisolone 1 g IV infusion on the first day and then 500 mg daily infusion (for 3 days)

treatment.name: tetracycline skin ointment daily
treatment.quote: After consultation regarding body burns, tetracycline skin ointment was given daily.

treatment.name: hemodialysis two times, 8 h each (days 1 and 3)
treatment.quote: He underwent hemodialysis two times, 8 h each time (the first and third day of hospitalization) due to a positive dithionite test and renal failure.

treatment.name: potassium chloride 15% (day 3, hypokalemia)
treatment.quote: On the third day of hospitalization, potassium chloride 15% was prescribed due to reported hypokalemia.

treatment.name: intubation and mechanical ventilation
treatment.quote: At this time, the patient was intubated and transferred to the ICU.

cases.outcome: died on the fourth day of hospitalization despite CPR
cases.outcome_quote: Finally, the cardio-respiratory arrest occurred, and the patient died despite cardiopulmonary resuscitation.
cases.notes: Developed sinus bradycardia with SpO2 35–40% on FiO2 100% before arrest; past history of methadone and opium inhalation addiction; laboratory table (Table 1) not present in text.
